subject: INLA with graph for Matern2d kernel

messages.author: ab78e227e394cf1d
messages.subject: INLA with graph for Matern2d kernel
parts:
Hi everyone,

I have a question regarding the graph option in INLA. When we do use a "matern" kernel in spatial random effect, can we add any additional graph structure on it? Is it meaningful for regular lattice or it is just concentrated for irregular cases?

If so, how is the parameters gonna to be estimated?
A small example is as follows for the random effect part

```
Y=c(1:20)
X=c(11:30)+rnorm(20,1,2)
Z=c(21:40)+rnorm(20,1,2)
W=c(21:40)+rnorm(20,1,2)
library(INLA)

model_graph=INLA::inla(Y~X*Z*W
                  +f(ID,
                    graph = adjacent,
                   model = "matern2d",nrow=4,ncol=5)
                 ,
                 family = "poisson",
           data=data.frame(X,Y,Z,W,ID=c(1:20)))

```
Alokesh.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA with graph for Matern2d kernel
parts:
You mean specifically the exp(-x^2/C) RBF kernel? (there are _many_
RBF kernels; all isotropic covariance kernels are radial basis
functions; I'm not sure why some of the literature pretends
otherwise...)
Since the exp(-x^2) kernel is essentially the infinite Markov order
limit case of Matern, it is one of the worst models, and generates
analytic functions as process realisations, so we haven't really
worked on that case. You should get very similar results with alpha >=
4 in 2D I think (smoothness >= 3). I believe the rSPDE package
supports construction of high order Matern models, so take a look at
that; https://cran.r-project.org/package=rSPDE (it uses the same
mesh/SPDE construction as the basic cases, but extends it to general
fractional operator orders)

Finn
